Casey.confusing: The dawn egg counts and the Kookaburra confusion were hard to track, since a visited Turkey pays its visitor and Blair's report was marked confused. Several players' egg stories didn't reconcile with what the rules say a visit should produce.
Casey.fun: Round 3 went well: as a Farm Hawk I cleared Blair, and the table converged on Finley, the Mouser, so the Farm side won.
Casey.change: Make the Storyteller's dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can check claims without guessing.
Casey.regret: In Round 1 I falsely claimed to be a Pigeon and then threw all five cards at Drew, a Farm player, which cost my team the round. I would stay quiet about my role and throw only low cards at the Meowfia suspect.

Drew.confusing: The Round 3 Sphinx night: I didn't realize Meowfia players couldn't see each other, so I couldn't tell who was lying about their Turkey claim. Whether a Tit guess that got no egg proved a player wasn't the Turkey was also unclear.
Drew.fun: Round 2 turned on Ellis contradicting their own story twice, and the table closed in on them in one clean day.
Drew.change: Make egg-count reporting more transparent, so players can verify visits without relying on each other's claimed roles.
Drew.regret: In Round 3 I threw my two highest cards at Ellis, a Farm player, which cost cards without helping. I should have thrown low cards at Finley to back the vote and kept my high cards banked.

Ellis.confusing: The dawn egg tokens versus the Turkey payout were hard to track, since a Turkey gets an egg from each visitor but the visitor's own nest doesn't change. I also couldn't tell whether a Pigeon's egg goes to the visited nest or the visitor's.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when the table converged on Finley's Mouser visit and Blair's collapse, and the Wink reasoning clicked for everyone at once. Finley's cards then went to my side's score pile.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn report state whose egg came from which visit, so a visitor can't mix up their own gain with the Turkey's payout.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I made up a Pigeon claim that I couldn't support, then threw five cards at Blair and lost my egg base. Instead I should have admitted I was the Sphinx and kept my cards, since a Meowfia with a clean story is harder to vote out.

Finley.confusing: The Wink timing: Blair collapsed right after my Mouser visit, so the table read it as my Wink, and nobody could tell a Wink from a visit-linked death. Also, Drew and Ellis both claimed Turkey, and I couldn't tell which one was lying.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when Ellis's story kept shifting from Pigeon to Turkey, and the table pinned them with the unexplained +1. Watching the Eagle counts line up against the claims was satisfying.
Finley.change: Make the Wink's use public, or at least show who winked, so a death can't be blamed on whoever visited that player just before.
Finley.regret: I winked Blair on day 3 when Blair was a Farm Falcon and the scoreboard leader, which wasted my Wink and left me exposed. I would hold the Wink for a Farm player pushing a vote on me or a clear Meowfia suspect.

review.title: The Easy Lynchings
review.headline: Three rounds, three Meowfia lynched, and Blair coasted to a win.
review.summary: Farm won every round. Each time the table piled onto a player whose story broke or who admitted to being a cat. Blair led from round 1 and added to the lead by throwing high cards at safe targets. The Meowfia could not cooperate because they did not know each other, and the one Wink was spent in a way that exposed its user.

rounds.recap: Casey (Mouser) claimed Pigeon, but Drew's nest did not move, so the claim broke. Casey would not explain. Everyone threw at Casey, who was eggsecuted. Casey threw all five cards at Drew and did not stop it. Farm won.

Ellis (Sphinx) claimed Pigeon, then said his +1 came from visiting the Turkey, then said he could not source it. Finley's Eagle report showed nobody else visited Ellis. Four players threw at Ellis. Casey, the other Meowfia, joined in. Blair banked 13 points.

Finley (Mouser) winked Blair on the first beat, then announced he was a Mouser and had visited Blair. That was almost a confession. Drew (Sphinx), his partner, claimed Turkey against the real Turkey and was shown false by Alex's Tit check. Drew still threw at Ellis, not Finley. Finley was eggsecuted and Farm won.

highlights.text: Casey's Pigeon claim fell apart against Drew's +0, and the whole table agreed on Casey in one beat.
Ellis's +1 had no source. Finley's Eagle report, 'nobody else visited Ellis', was the clue that sank him.
Finley winked Blair, then said in his own words that he was a Mouser who had visited Blair, and so gave himself away.
Alex's Tit guess on Drew got no egg. That cleanly disproved Drew's Turkey claim and gave Farm something solid to use.

confusions.what: Claimed Pigeon and said he visited Drew. Drew had already been seen as the Kookaburra, and a Pigeon visit would have given Drew an egg. The claim was easy to disprove.
Claimed Pigeon but said his own +1 came from it. A Pigeon lays the egg in the target's nest, not his own. He then said the egg came from visiting the Turkey, which he had also described wrongly.
Said openly that he was a Mouser and had visited Blair. He then expected the table to still treat him as a plausible Farm player.
Claimed Turkey while Ellis had already claimed it. He was also the only Meowfia who knew Blair was the Falcon, and he did nothing with that.
Said a Turkey visit 'would have given you the egg from me'. This is garbled. A Turkey lays the egg in the visitor's nest.
Said Ellis's Pigeon egg went to Alex, and used it to explain his own +2. A Pigeon visit does lay an egg in Alex's nest, but this was not checked against Drew's egg that also went to Alex.

worked: Egg tokens and nest changes gave real evidence. Casey's Pigeon claim in round 1 and Ellis's unsourced +1 in round 2 could be checked against other players' counts.
Alex's Tit check in round 3 was a clean, fair clue. It disproved a Turkey claim and created a real conflict between Ellis and Drew.
The Wink killing Blair in round 3 was a good dramatic moment. It showed that death removes a voice but not the thrown cards.
problems: Meowfia never won. Without knowing each other they could not coordinate, and every round ended with one Meowfia lynched by an easy consensus. Consider giving Meowfia a way to find each other or a stronger night action.

The first beats made the vote a foregone conclusion. In rounds 1 and 2 the table settled on one target within two beats and CAW ended the day. The three-CAW rule made the end quick, so there was little time for doubt.

The Wink revealed its owner. Finley winked and then claimed Mouser the same day. Players cannot be told apart if the Wink user speaks like this, so the rule should make winking carry less information or have a cost.

The scoring snowballs. Blair led after round 1 and banked high cards safely each round, finishing with 32. Trailing players had little to gain from deviating, so the standings never shaped the play. Consider capping banked values or adding a catch-up rule.

Meowfia often threw at their own partner or at nobody useful. Casey and Drew's votes did not change any outcome, so the 1-or-2 Meowfia rule added little. Round 1 and 2 secretly had one Meowfia each, so the hidden count never mattered.
